newsitem.title: USA: Britannica to start selling through retail stores.
newsitem.headline: Britannica to start selling through retail stores.

text.p: Encyclopaedia Britannica Inc. said Thursday it will make its 32-volume encyclopaedia, traditionally distributed through direct mail and in-home sales, available to retail bookstores beginning this fall.
The sets will be distributed by Merriam-Webster Inc., a subsidiary of Encyclopaedia Britannica.
The company has been testing retail distribution for six months. Under the retail plan, Encyclopaedia Britannica will still ship the sets directly to customers.

Purchased by Swiss investor Jacob Safra in 1996 from the University of Chicago, Encyclopaedia Britannica was established in Scotland in 1768. It has been printed in its 32-volume form since 1985 and had sales of $407,000 in 1995, the last year figures were available.
The company would not say what portion of sales it hopes to gain through retail store sales.
